articles.title: ‘He’s a good man’: George Clooney defends Mark Ruffalo in Paramount-Warner Bros merger row
articles.summary: ‘I worry whenever big companies are consolidating,’ Clooney said at Venice film festival, supporting Ruffalo’s right to criticise the deal amid antisemitism accusations.
body: George Clooney has defended Mark Ruffalo’s right to criticise the proposed $111bn Paramount takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, saying he is concerned about the consequences of further consolidation in Hollywood.

Speaking in Venice ahead of receiving the festival’s Golden Lion for lifetime achievement, Clooney said he supported Ruffalo’s “ability to speak freely” about the proposed merger, while expressing his own doubts about the deal.
“I worry when a big company swallows up another company,” Clooney said. “I always worry whenever big companies are consolidating because it means a lot of people are going to lose their jobs.”

Ruffalo has emerged as one of the most outspoken opponents of the Paramount-Warner Bros deal. In a social media post last month, the Marvel star attacked the proposed merger over its potential consequences for Hollywood, while also turning his criticism on the family behind Paramount. David Ellison, the company’s chief executive, is the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, and Ruffalo accused the Ellison family of being complicit the “genocide” of Palestinians, arguing that it was “built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle”.

articles.title: The Eyes Wide Shut conspiracy theory: did someone cut a crucial 20 minutes from Kubrick’s final movie?
articles.summary: For years some have claimed a key part of the thriller was excised after the director’s sudden death – and that it provided clues to the real-life behaviour of rich predators. Now, his daughter has spoken out. Name: The Eyes Wide Shut conspiracy.
body: Age: The erotic psychological thriller Eyes Wide Shut starring Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman (married at the time, though that isn’t so important now) was released in 1999.
Stanley Kubrick, no? yes. It was the great film-maker’s final movie. He died of a heart attack just days after screening his final cut to Warner Bros. His sudden death is what started it all.
Oooh, go on. OK, so there are rumours that the studio cut 20 minutes of the film after his death, including an alternative ending.

Why would they do that? It was too dark apparently, even by Kubrick’s standards. The theory goes that in Kubrick’s original, Cruise and Kidman’s characters sacrificed their own daughter to a child sexual abuse ring.

articles.title: Maggie Gyllenhaal says film industry has a ‘systemic problem’ with sexism
articles.summary: Speaking at the opening of the Venice film festival, the actor-director addressed why the jury of which she is chair will only be shown two films made by female film-makers.
body: Maggie Gyllenhaal said there is a “systemic problem” that explains why only two female directors are in the running for the Golden Lion at the Venice film festival this year.
“It’s harder for women to get films financed,” said the actor-director, who is heading up the jury of the world’s oldest cinema showcase this year.

“Could it be possible that the things that women, having had a different experience of being alive in the world, want to make movies about are not always deemed high art?” added Gyllenhaal, whose directing debut The Lost Daughter won a best screenplay prize at Venice in 2021. “Who decides what’s good? Who decides what is valuable?”

The artistic directors of the film festival have faced criticism since the original lineup revealed that that only one of the 20 contenders for the top prize was by a female film-maker, Danish-Egyptian director May el-Toukhy’s Woman Unknown.

articles.title: ‘He was always a bit of a groundbreaker’: David Bowie enters a new dimension in ‘extended reality’ documentary
articles.summary: Hundreds of unseen images of the star feature at the Venice film festival, alongside virtual worlds exploring wildfires, wolves and the birth of stars. David Bowie shares the bill with starmen, firefighters and Walt Disney wolves at the 10th anniversary edition of Venice Immersive, the film…
body: Venice Immersive’s 10th birthday marks a milestone for an event which aims to provide a bridge between emergent technology and traditional narrative cinema. But the programme’s organisers are at pains to emphasise the ongoing scope of a project that has in recent years prompted similar sections at the Cannes, Geneva and Toronto film festivals. “This is not a retrospective,” declares the official festival blurb that welcomes guests to the island. It almost sounds like a warning.

“This is such a fast-evolving medium,” says Liz Rosenthal, Venice Immersive’s co-curator. “We’re basically witnessing new forms of art being crafted in real time. So we’re already looking forward to the next 10 years. I think we’re very much at a turning point in terms of the platforms and technology that’s available – and this in turn will shape the nature of the storytelling itself.”

articles.title: ‘I’m Hoping to See Sydney Sweeney’: Meet the Superfans Who Camp Out All Night for Celebrity Sightings at Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: It’s 11:30 p.m. on Tuesday, and 19-year-old Delsina Desanctes is standing outside the Palazzo de Cinema — the iconic venue where the Venice Film Festival takes place — surrounded by umbrellas, suitcases, sleeping bags and even a tent.
body: Desanctes isn’t fazed by the brutal heat or hours of waiting around. This is her seventh year in the thick of the action, and she’s gotten good at passing the time. In fact, she’s not even all that interested in the stars. She’s saving a spot for her celebrity-obsessed best friend, who is back at their hotel taking a disco nap before the fun begins.

“I smoke. I love talking to people, so the time passes,” Desanctes says. “I didn’t eat or drink all day today, so tomorrow I’m going to reset. It’s crazy, but it’s the only time of year I’m going to do that.”

Michele, a 29-year-old Italian who has attended the festival for the past decade, took time off work so he could get to the Palazzo by 6 p.m. on Tuesday. It’s a lot of time and effort, sure, but he learned the hard way that showing up any later meant he’d get a lame placement on the carpet. If you don’t have a decent view of the action, you certainly won’t be able to score any autographs or selfies.
“Last year, I arrived at 9 p.m. the day before, and it was too late. I was on the last part of the red carpet,” he says. “If I got here tomorrow, I’d be in the third or fourth row.”

articles.title: ‘Harry Potter’ Trailer: Harry Wears the Sorting Hat, Tries Quidditch and Puts on Invisibility Cloak in HBO’s TV Remake
articles.summary: HBO’s “Harry Potter” series has released another trailer, giving a peek into the new take on the Wizarding World as it makes its way to TV. Newcomer Dominic McLaughlin stars as Harry Potter, the 11-year old wizard previously brought to life by Daniel Radcliffe.
body: The new show is a massive undertaking by HBO, which is adapting all seven of author J.K. Rowling’s books into seven seasons of TV. The first eight-episode season takes on “The Sorcerer’s Stone” and is set to release on Christmas. The show also snagged an early Season 2 renewal in May, which will follow “The Chamber of Secrets.”

The cast includes John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, the headmaster of Hogwarts; Janet McTeer as Prof. McGonagall; Paapa Essiedu as Prof. Snape; Nick Frost as Hagrid; Luke Thallon as Prof. Quirrell; Paul Whitehouse as Argus Filch; Bertie Carvel as Cornelius Fudge; Johnny Flynn as Lucius Malfoy and more. Many young actors are getting their first major starts on the series as well. Lox Pratt is Draco Malfoy; Leo Earley as Seamus Finnegan; Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom; Gracie Cochrane as Ginny Weasley; and Elijah Oshin as Dean Thomas.

body: Having launched the film ahead of the American Film Market in 2025, Mister Smith Entertainment will continue international sales at the upcoming TIFF market, where they will debut new footage to foreign buyers.

In “The Turning Door,” a little girl finds a mysterious box hidden in her parent’s closet. As it grows into an open door, she falls through to another world called The Turning. There, she must embark on a grand adventure of old magic, strange creatures, new lands, alchemy, dreams and songs, all to return home and save her parents.

The film is produced by Christine D’Souza of After Hours, Hunter Hall and Bateman of Maere Studios (“The Wanting Mare,” “An Almost Christmas Story”) and Laura Rister for Esme Grace Pictures (“Ferrari,” “The Tale”). Production is currently underway.

articles.title: Lizzo 'grateful' after judge dismisses lawsuit against production company
articles.summary: The About Damn Time singer says she is "relieved" at the outcome and will "continue to fight" every claim.
body: US pop star Lizzo has spoken out after the remaining claims in a lawsuit against her production company were thrown out by a US district judge.

The singer's former wardrobe assistant Asha Daniels alleged she had been subjected to "degradation, forced physical labor, denial of medical care, sexual harassment, and racial harassment" while briefly working for Big Grrrl Big Touring in 2023.
In 2024, judge Aenlle-Rocha ruled that Daniels could not sue the Grammy winner as an individual, but Big Grrrl Big Touring Inc remained a defendant.

In his ruling this week, he said the former wardrobe assistant did not identify any conduct by company employees that would demonstrate "general hostility to women in the workplace" or "disparate treatment of men and women".

articles.title: King Charles, Macron and Burnham to preview Bayeux Tapestry display
articles.summary: British and French leaders will be at the British Museum to see the exhibition of the historic Bayeux Tapestry.
body: King Charles, French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham are to preview one of the blockbuster cultural events of the year, when they get to view the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum.
The visit on Wednesday comes ahead of the medieval tapestry going on public display in London from 10 September.
The 70m (230ft) tapestry, originally embroidered in England but kept for centuries in France, tells the story of the Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
President Macron said the loan of the national treasure until July 2027 was a "powerful symbol" of the close ties between the UK and France.

articles.title: Meryl Streep, Laura Poitras Join ‘My Undesirable Friends: Part II’ as Exec Producers (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Julia Loktev’s follow-up to her 2024 documentary follows independent Russian journalists forced to flee Moscow after Putin's government declares them "foreign agents."
body: Meryl Streep and Oscar-winning documentarian Laura Poitras ( Citzenfour ) have come onboard as executive producers on upcoming documentary My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile, Julia Loktev’s follow up to her acclaimed 2024 doc My Undesirable Friends: Part I – The Last Air in Moscow about independent journalists under fire in Russia.

Poitras called Loktev’s film “an epic in the tradition of the great writers of the country her family emigrated from – Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, and Chekhov. Documenting history unfolding in real time, Julia takes us inside the intimate and beautiful world of a group of young journalists – mostly women – as they risk their lives, and go into exile in pursuit of the truth. I am honored to stand alongside Julia and her many extraordinarily courageous and desirable friends.”

My Undesirable Friends: Part I – The Last Air in Moscow won the Gotham Independent Film Awards, the New York Film Critics Circle, Los Angeles Film Critics Association, and National Society of Film Critics awards for best documentary.
